segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers mostly find the gentle physical exfoliation preferable to chemical options and report soft, nourished skin afterward, though several caution to use a light touch since the rice grains can feel rough or even mildly irritating if rubbed hard; one reviewer with extra-sensitive skin experienced a brief tingling on her nose and suggests this mask may not suit very reactive skin.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry or dry-flaky skin report the mask hydrates rather than tightens, describing skin as plump, soft, and free of the tight or flaky feeling they had before, including one who was skeptical a physical scrub would suit dry skin but was pleasantly surprised.
segments.combination: One reviewer describes the mask as suitable for combination skin as part of a broader skin-type endorsement.
segments.oily: The same reviewer suggests it also works for oily skin, particularly for an evening/PM use.

concerns.dehydration: Hydration is the most consistently reported benefit: reviewers across skin types describe the mask leaving skin plump, soft, and moisturized rather than tight or stripped, including several with dry or flaky skin who specifically note it didn't dry them out.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with extra-sensitive skin experienced a tingling, mildly irritating sensation on her nose after use that subsided within minutes; most other reviewers, including several with sensitive skin, report no irritation, though many caution that the rice grains can scratch the skin if rubbed too hard rather than applied gently on damp skin.
concerns.spots: Brightening and a more even skin tone are widely reported after use, described as an immediate effect by several reviewers and attributed to both the physical exfoliation and the rice's vitamin content; no reviewer in this set reports the opposite.
concerns.blemishes: A couple of reviewers who deal with clogged pores report the mask helped calm congestion in those areas, and one specifically notes it didn't cause any breakouts, suggesting it may suit acne-prone skin as well, though this is based on limited direct testimony.

It's easy to apply using a silicon brush. The grains are not too harsh now because I read some reviews before that the grains of the old formula were too harsh and had some sharp rice hulls. Despite its new formulation, if you have extra sensitive skin, this may not be for you. I experienced a tingling sensation on both sides of my nose, which I found irritating because I wanted to scratch it out (but I didn't, don't worry) and I'm glad that it subsided in a few minutes. extraits.texte: For someone with sensitive skin I generally prefer a good gentle physical exfoliation over chemical ones to avoid irritation. This rice mask is very nourishing with varying sizes of grains. I use this mask about once a week. I just leave it on the face for a while and when I am ready to wash it off, I'd wet my fingertips and do a few gentle circles on the face. Immediately after washing the mask off, my face looks brighter and oh so much smoother! This mask is my mom's favorite, she tried it once and took it from me. Sometimes the rice husk pieces can be bit too rough if you rub too hard.
